newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch DAF bondholders lose claim against ABN AMRO.
newsitem.headline: Dutch DAF bondholders lose claim against ABN AMRO.

text.p: A Dutch court on Wednesday rejected two legal actions by bond investors in failed Dutch truckmaker DAF NV against ABN AMRO and other banks.
The Amsterdam District Court dismissed claims by the Nederlandsche Trust-Maatschappij, the bondholders' trustee, over information in a prospectus for the bond issue in 1988.
"We are, of course, very happy about it," ABN AMRO spokesman Theo van Dijk said after the verdict.
The trustee alleged AMRO AMRO published misleading information in the prospectus for the 150 million guilder issue. DAF went bankrupt in 1993 before being resurrected and sold.
The bonds plunged to a third of their nominal value after the truckmaker collapsed.
In the legal action, which began in 1994, the bond investors claimed they were entitled to some of the funds raised from asset sales after the bankruptcy, which went to creditor banks.
A spokesman for the trustee said it planned to appeal against the decision but declined to elaborate on the reasons.
